WITH p AS (SELECT $1::text AS ref, $2::text AS cancel_reason),
tgt AS (SELECT a.* FROM appointment a JOIN p ON a.ref = p.ref),
upd AS (
  UPDATE appointment a
     SET status = 'cancelled', cancelled_at = now(),
         cancel_reason = p.cancel_reason, updated_at = now()
    FROM p
   WHERE a.ref = p.ref AND a.status = 'confirmed'
  RETURNING a.*
)
SELECT json_build_object(
  'found',        (SELECT count(*) FROM tgt) > 0,
  'prior_status', (SELECT status FROM tgt),
  'cancelled',    (SELECT count(*) FROM upd) > 0,
  'freed', (SELECT json_build_object(
              'ref', u.ref, 'stylist_id', u.stylist_id, 'stylist_name', st.name,
              'service_id', u.service_id, 'service_name', sv.name,
              'client_id', u.client_id, 'client_name', c.name,
              'starts_at_utc',   to_char(u.starts_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC','YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS"Z"'),
              'ends_at_utc',     to_char(u.ends_at   AT TIME ZONE 'UTC','YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS"Z"'),
              'starts_at_local', to_char(u.starts_at AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Manila','YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI'),
              'ends_at_local',   to_char(u.ends_at   AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Manila','HH24:MI'))
            FROM upd u
            JOIN stylist st ON st.id = u.stylist_id
            JOIN service sv ON sv.id = u.service_id
            JOIN client  c  ON c.id  = u.client_id)
) AS result;

## 22 · cancel booking

**In** `{booking_ref, cancel_reason?}`
**Out** `{ok:true, data:{freed:{stylist_id, service_id, starts_at_*, ends_at_*, client_*}}}`

The `UPDATE … WHERE status='confirmed'` means two racing cancels produce exactly one winner. The freed window is what phase 3 offers on to the waitlist.
